title: Translator for OpenAI-style tools -> Redwood function surface with schema reconciliation & streaming hooks
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Customers are using OpenAI-style 'tools' payloads (name + JSON Schema params + function_call hints) while large parts of Redwood runtime and older SDKs expect a different 'function' surface (snake_case arg names, positional semantics in some clients, and an existing function registry). This mismatch causes: name collisions, parameter casing mismatches, incompatible schemas, broken streaming behavior when the model selects function_call vs standard text streaming, and confusing telemetry.

Goal: Implement a translator layer inside the API gateway/runtime that accepts OpenAI-style tool requests and reliably maps them to Redwood function invocations (and back). The translator must preserve streaming semantics (events for start/arg-chunk/end), reconcile parameter schema differences with coercions and validations, emit deprecation/compatibility telemetry, and allow per-customer mapping overrides. It must also provide a clear opt-out path for customers who want raw mode.
acceptance_criteria: Translator layer accepts incoming OpenAI-style payloads and returns identical observable results for downstream Redwood function handlers compared to a handwritten equivalent mapping (behavioral parity).
Handles name normalization rules and exposes admin mapping overrides (per-tenant) via console or config file.

Performs parameter coercion for common mismatches (kebab-case, camelCase -> snake_case; strings -> numbers when unambiguous; missing optional params) and rejects invalid payloads with structured error codes.

Preserves streaming when the model chooses function_call: events emitted: TOOL_CALL_START, TOOL_ARG_CHUNK, TOOL_CALL_END, TOOL_CALL_ERROR and these are plumbed to existing streaming SDKs (JS/Python) without breaking current text-stream flows.
Records telemetry: mapping decisions, coercions applied, name collisions, deprecated name usage, and adds trace IDs linking request -> translated invocation -> function execution.
Feature gate: translator is toggleable per-tenant; default is opt-in for enterprise customers during rollout; must support canary routing for 1% / 10% / 100%.
Unit + integration tests for 80+ schema permutations; e2e test that invokes a sample function via: (1) OpenAI-style tool, (2) Redwood legacy function signature, assert identical responses and logs.
Documentation updated: API reference examples for JS + Python, a migration guide with recommended renames and a warning table for ambiguities.
Security: mapping and coercion logic reviewed and approved by security (no path traversal or injection attack surface); secrets not leaked through schema validation errors.
tech_notes: Design: translator is a runtime plugin that sits in the API gateway layer before routing to the runtime. We rejected compile-time rewriting because we need per-tenant overrides and rapid rollbacks.

Name resolution precedence: 1) explicit tenant mapping (console) 2) tool 'name' exact match to registered function 3) normalized name (lowercase, '-' and '.' -> '_') 4) generated alias with numeric suffix on collision (emit deprecation event).

Parameter mapping algorithm: use incoming JSON Schema (tool.params) to build a mapping table; prefer structural matches (same keys with different casing) and coerce basic primitives. For ambiguous numeric/string conversions require explicit mapping or fail with 400 + reason.

Streaming: implement an event wrapper that maps model tool-call stream tokens into structured events to downstream function handler. Keep a minimal in-memory buffer to avoid token reassembly across multiple shards; design to be backpressure-aware for high-throughput scenarios.
Performance: the translator should add <2ms median overhead for typical small-tool calls; implement fast paths for exact-match name + param identity to avoid schema validation cost on hot paths.
Observability: add structured logs at INFO for mapping decisions and ERROR for any rejection. Expose a per-tenant dashboard in Console for mapping hits/misses and top coercions.
Security: validate schema size (max 64KB) and disallow 'additionalProperties: false' bypass techniques. Sanitize error messages that include user-provided property names.
Rollout plan: behind feature flag at gw-layer; canary 1% -> 10% -> 100% with health checks: success rate, latency delta, function error rates, and undefined coercions metric.
Backward compatibility: provide ?raw=true query param to skip translation and pass payload untouched to runtime for advanced/legacy users.
decisions: Use runtime plugin vs compile-time transformation to allow per-tenant mappings and easier rollbacks.
Emit structured events for streaming rather than flattening to text; this preserves downstream function semantics.
Coercion policy: apply safe coercions (case transforms, hyphen/underscore) automatically; require explicit mapping for lossy type conversions.
Persist mapping metadata as versioned objects in config-store (not in code) so we can audit changes and revert if needed.
Do not auto-create functions from tools. Translator maps to existing registered function names only; if no match and tenant allows, return 404 with suggestion list.
Collision handling: when two functions collide after normalization, mark both as ambiguous and require explicit tenant mapping; generate a mapping recommendation file in Console.
updates: 2026-03-09: Spike completed. Prototype translator implemented in a sidecar using existing runtime registry. Performance baseline measured: median 1.6ms extra with full schema validation (small schemas).
2026-03-11: PR #4897 opened for runtime plugin scaffolding. Design reviewed with PM (Sofia Tran) and Security (Kyle O'Neal). Security requested explicit size limits on schemas and sanitized errors.
2026-03-12: UX/Console team proposed a mapping UI flow: suggest mappings, allow approve/reject, and show last 90-day hits. Assigned follow-up EPIC to PM (PM-412).

2026-03-13: Edge case found: some SDKs send positional args encoded in single 'arguments' string field; added heuristic to parse common patterns and emit warning telemetry. Needs opt-in mapping; marked as TODO to avoid accidental behavior changes.

2026-03-14: Performance optimization committed: add fast-path bypass when tool.name exact matches function registry and request has 'params' null or small; unit tests expanded. Planning canary rollout next week.
Next steps: finish integration tests for streaming event plumbing, add Console mapping UI backend endpoint, and schedule security review follow-up for schema sanitizer.
